title: Forces and Equilibrium Module 1 Lesson 2: Resultant Magnitude Direction custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, numerical values and physical configurations are original; mapped Cambridge past-paper evidence informs cognitive demand and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Two perpendicular forces act on a particle: a force of $12\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis and a force of $5\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R$, and find the angle $\theta$ that the resultant makes with the positive $x$-axis, giving your angle correct to 1 decimal place.

The horizontal and vertical components of a resultant force $\mathbf{R}$ are $R_x = -20\text{ N}$ and $R_y = 15\text{ N}$ respectively. Calculate the magnitude of $\mathbf{R}$, and find the acute angle $\theta$ that $\mathbf{R}$ makes with the negative $x$-axis, giving the angle correct to 1 decimal place.

A force has horizontal component $X = 24\text{ N}$ in the positive $x$-direction and vertical component $Y = -7\text{ N}$ in the negative $y$-direction. Calculate the magnitude of the force, and find the acute angle that it makes below the positive $x$-axis, giving the angle correct to 1 decimal place.

Two forces of magnitudes $8\text{ N}$ and $15\text{ N}$ act at right angles to each other on a point $O$. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, and determine the acute angle between the resultant force and the $8\text{ N}$ force, giving your answer correct to 1 decimal place.

Two forces act at a point $O$: a force of $10\text{ N}$ directed due East (along the positive $x$-axis) and a force of $14\text{ N}$ directed at an angle of $60^\circ$ North of East. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A force of $20\text{ N}$ acts along the positive $x$-axis, and a second force of magnitude $P\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis. Given that the resultant of these two forces acts entirely along the $y$-axis, calculate the value of $P$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Two coplanar forces act at a point $O$. Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ has magnitude $15\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $40^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis. Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ has magnitude $20\text{ N}$ and acts at an angle of $65^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis (in the fourth quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the total component $X$ in the $x$-direction and the total component $Y$ in the $y$-direction of the resultant force, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, and find the acute angle that the resultant makes with the positive $x$-axis, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$: a force of $30\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, a force of $40\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis, and a force of $50\text{ N}$ acting at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis (in the third quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the net component $X$ in the $x$-direction and the net component $Y$ in the $y$-direction of the three forces, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, and find the acute angle that the resultant makes with the negative $x$-axis, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$. Force $\mathbf{F}_1$ has magnitude $25\text{ N}$ and acts at an acute angle $\alpha$ above the positive $x$-axis, where $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$. Force $\mathbf{F}_2$ has magnitude $13\text{ N}$ and acts at an acute angle $\beta$ above the negative $x$-axis (in the second quadrant), where $\tan\beta = \frac{5}{12}$. Force $\mathbf{F}_3$ has magnitude $14\text{ N}$ and acts along the negative $y$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: By using exact values for the trigonometric ratios of $\alpha$ and $\beta$, calculate the exact net horizontal component $X$ and the exact net vertical component $Y$ of the three forces.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, and find the acute angle that the resultant makes with the positive $x$-axis, giving the angle correct to 1 decimal place.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: An additional force of magnitude $F\text{ N}$ is applied to the point $O$ along the negative $x$-axis. Given that the new resultant force acts entirely in the positive $y$-direction, state the value of $F$ and the magnitude of the new resultant force.

questions.prompt: Coplanar forces of magnitudes $18\text{ N}$, $24\text{ N}$ and $30\text{ N}$ act at a point $O$. The $18\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $25^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis (first quadrant). The $24\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $50^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis (second quadrant). The $30\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $35^\circ$ below the negative $x$-axis (third quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Show clearly how the forces are resolved to find the components of the resultant force in the $x$-direction and $y$-direction, and calculate these components correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, and find the acute angle that the resultant makes with the negative $x$-axis, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces of magnitudes $32\text{ N}$, $20\text{ N}$ and $P\text{ N}$ act at a point $O$. The $32\text{ N}$ force acts along the positive $x$-axis. The $20\text{ N}$ force acts at an angle of $60^\circ$ above the negative $x$-axis (second quadrant). The force of magnitude $P\text{ N}$ acts at an angle of $30^\circ$ below the positive $x$-axis (fourth quadrant).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant of the three forces acts entirely in the positive $x$-direction (so that its vertical component is zero), calculate the exact value of $P$ in surd form, and state its value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using the exact value of $P$ found in part (a), calculate the magnitude of the resultant force.

questions.prompt: A small block of mass $m = 5\text{ kg}$ rests on a smooth horizontal table at the origin $O$. Three horizontal forces are applied to the block simultaneously: a force $\mathbf{F}_1$ of magnitude $45\text{ N}$ acting at an angle of $25^\circ$ North of East, a force $\mathbf{F}_2$ of magnitude $30\text{ N}$ acting at an angle of $50^\circ$ North of West, and a force $\mathbf{F}_3$ of magnitude $28\text{ N}$ directed due South. Take the positive $x$-axis to point due East and the positive $y$-axis to point due North.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the component of the resultant force in the East ($x$) direction and the component of the resultant force in the North ($y$) direction, giving each value correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the magnitude of the resultant force, and determine its direction as a three-figure bearing, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The block is released from rest from point $O$ at time $t = 0$. Given that the table is smooth so that no frictional forces act, calculate the speed of the block at $t = 4.0\text{ s}$, and the distance it has traveled from $O$ during this time.

questions.prompt: Three coplanar forces act at a point $O$: a force of magnitude $60\text{ N}$ along the positive $x$-axis, a force of magnitude $80\text{ N}$ acting at an angle $\theta$ above the positive $x$-axis (where $0^\circ < \theta < 180^\circ$), and a force of magnitude $40\text{ N}$ along the positive $y$-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write down expressions in terms of $\theta$ for the total component $X$ in the $x$-direction and the total component $Y$ in the $y$-direction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Given that the resultant of the three forces acts entirely in the positive $y$-direction (so that $X = 0$), find the value of $\theta$, and calculate the corresponding magnitude of the resultant force, giving each answer correct to 3 significant figures.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Suppose instead that $\theta$ can vary over the range $0^\circ \leqslant \theta \leqslant 180^\circ$. By considering the square of the resultant magnitude, $R^2 = X^2 + Y^2$, determine the value of $\theta$ for which the resultant force has its maximum possible magnitude, and calculate this maximum magnitude correct to 3 significant figures.
